Apple has made its submissions regarding the issue of fees for transactions outside the App Store in the Epic Games litigation. Here are the relevant details.

Apple submits proposal on App Store external transaction commissions

After multiple requests to halt the district court proceedings — which will determine whether and how Apple can charge commissions on transactions outside its IAP system within the App Store — Apple has finally submitted its proposal outlining the proposed fee structure.

Apple submitted its proposal shortly after the Supreme Court denied Apple's request to halt the lower court proceedings. Apple had hoped to suspend the relevant proceedings so that the Supreme Court could hear its case; in that case, Apple could potentially be held in contempt of court for charging a 27% commission on transactions outside the App Store. Previously, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers had issued an injunction requiring Apple to allow developers to direct users to other purchase methods.

Apple argued in both the district court and subsequently to the Supreme Court that the court's ruling could affect the outcome of the fee determination process, and therefore the relevant proceedings should be suspended before the court makes a decision. However, the Supreme Court denied Apple's request, allowing the district court proceedings to continue during the trial.

Therefore, Apple has now submitted its proposal, with the suggested fees as follows:

Standard apps charge 15% (such apps currently pay a 30% in-app purchase ("IAP") commission);

Apple stated: "Factual and expert evidence regarding the above proposed commission rates have also been submitted simultaneously." The company added:

Apple further pointed out that its "proposed external link commission can also be compared with commissions from other competing app stores," including Google Play, Samsung Galaxy Store, and Amazon's Android App Marketplace.

The company also noted: "Google Play Store's standard external link fee structure is: standard rate 20%, program rate 15%, subscription rate 10% — these rates are also agreed by Epic."

Apple stated that it still believes the fee determination process should be suspended pending the outcome of the Supreme Court case, and added that the submission of this proposal is purely in compliance with Judge Gonzalez Rogers's instructions.

The company also noted that the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals has overturned the district court's blanket injunction on commissions for external link transactions, and stated that such commissions would only be problematic if they effectively constituted a backdoor ban.

After Apple submitted its proposal, Epic can now respond, and Apple is expected to submit its arguments to the Supreme Court before September 14.
